q: Oxidation and reduction reactions involve the transfer of oxygen atoms, or hydrogen atoms, electrons, or change in oxidation numbers.
e: This is the comprehensive definition of oxidation and reduction reactions.

q: When a substance gains oxygen in a chemical reaction, it is oxidised.
e: Gain of oxygen is the classical definition of oxidation.

q: When a substance gains oxygen in a chemical reaction, it is reduced.
e: When a substance gains oxygen, it is oxidised, not reduced.

q: When a substance loses oxygen in a chemical reaction, it is reduced.
e: Loss of oxygen is the classical definition of reduction.

q: When a substance loses hydrogen in a chemical reaction, it is oxidised.
e: Loss of hydrogen is a definition of oxidation in terms of hydrogen transfer.

q: When a substance loses hydrogen in a chemical reaction, it is reduced.
e: When a substance loses hydrogen, it is oxidised, not reduced.

q: When a substance gains hydrogen in a chemical reaction, it is reduced.
e: Gain of hydrogen is a definition of reduction in terms of hydrogen transfer.

q: Oxygen belongs to a class of electronegative elements and hydrogen belongs to electropositive elements.
e: This classification extends the concepts of oxidation and reduction to electronegative and electropositive elements.

q: Oxidation is the addition of oxygen (or electronegative element) to a substance.
e: This is the extended definition of oxidation based on electronegative elements.

q: Reduction is the removal of oxygen (or electronegative element) from a substance.
e: This is the extended definition of reduction based on electronegative elements.

q: Oxidation is the removal of hydrogen (or electropositive element) from a substance.
e: This is the extended definition of oxidation based on electropositive elements.

q: Reduction is the addition of hydrogen (or electropositive element) to a substance.
e: This is the extended definition of reduction based on electropositive elements.

q: Oxidation is the loss of electrons by an element, compound or ion.
e: This is the definition of oxidation in terms of electron transfer.

q: Oxidation is the gain of electrons by an element, compound or ion.
e: Oxidation is the loss of electrons; gain of electrons is reduction.

q: Reduction is the gain of electrons by an element, compound or ion.
e: This is the definition of reduction in terms of electron transfer.

q: Any element which increases in oxidation number is said to be oxidised.
e: An increase in oxidation number indicates oxidation.

q: Any element which decreases in oxidation number is said to be oxidised.
e: Any element which decreases in oxidation number is said to be reduced, not oxidised.

q: Any element which decreases in oxidation number is said to be reduced.
e: A decrease in oxidation number indicates reduction.

q: In the reaction of chlorine and hydrogen sulphide, hydrogen sulphide loses hydrogen and it is oxidised.
e: Hydrogen sulphide loses hydrogen to form sulphur, hence it is oxidised.

q: In the reaction of hydrogen and chlorine, chlorine gains hydrogen and it is reduced.
e: Chlorine gains hydrogen to form hydrogen chloride, hence it is reduced.
